note: The open world as it runs (roadmap items 39, 45, 48, 49, 50, 52; core/game/game_sandbox.gd). The heir's tiles, the creatures kept round them and the companions' threats are numbers here, not in code. Text is here too, so the screen and the log say the same thing.

levels.note: Creature levels in the open world (core/game/game_levels.gd). A creature's level is max(1, round(heir level * ratio * the place's danger)), the ratio drawn from `bands` (weight, then a range) on a hash of the dynasty seed and the spawn tile, never the dynasty's dice. `con_below` is where a creature's level / the heir's level puts it on the scale (the first band it is below; the last band takes the rest). `con_xp` is the share of a foe's xp it gives and `con_gold` the share of its gold it carries. `flee_bands` are the bands whose foes are fearful: below `flee_hp_share` of their health each of their turns they run with chance `flee_chance` and give no reward. `mark` is a character shown beside the level so colour is never the only cue; `color` is a Kit colour token (dim, good, text, accent, bad). Only fights begun from the open world's contact use any of this.

smoke.note: Smoke pots (core/game/game_smoke.gd). Using one lights a cloud on the heir's tile: for `seconds` of the world clock, nothing spawns within `radius` tiles of it, creatures inside it give up the chase and are driven out (at `drive` times their own speed, like a fleeing creature), and a creature outside cannot start a fight with a heir inside. `item` is the pot's id in items.json.

text.lit: {heir} breaks a smoke pot: a grey cloud rolls out over the ground.
text.indoors: Smoke pots are for the open ground, not indoors.
text.upstairs: Smoke pots are for the ground floor.
text.fight: Not in the middle of a fight.
text.already: The smoke here is still thick: {left} left.

feel.note: How walking looks and feels (ui/play/glide.gd, ui/play/move_marker.gd; drawing only, nothing here changes a rule). run_multiplier: how much faster the heir walks while the run key (world_run, Shift) is held; it costs nothing. The heir is drawn gliding between tiles by a smooth-damp over heir_smooth_seconds (a creature, companion or villager over other_smooth_seconds; 0 is no gliding), capped at max_speed_tiles a second, and snaps at once when the real position jumps by more than snap_tiles. A stride is step_tiles long: each one lifts the figure by bob_tiles of a tile (full at bob_full_speed tiles a second, none under bob_min_speed) and tells of a footstep when it falls, heard within hear_tiles of the heir. An entry not drawn for forget_frames frames is forgotten. marker: the mark where a click or tap walks to, which fades over fade_seconds on arriving or cancel_fade_seconds when a key or the stick ends the walk, pulsing every pulse_seconds, radius_tiles wide, line_px thick. Reduced motion: no gliding, no bob, no pulse, no fade.

tiles.note: The open world drawn as tile chunks (ui/play/tile_view.gd). px is a tile's size in the atlas, chunk the tiles to a TileMapLayer, keep the chunks kept beyond the view. Each kind (a biome, water, a built piece) has a colour; a stand-in for sprite art, which replaces the atlas and nothing else. Trees, herb patches, bone piles and outcrops (GameWorldGen's nodes) and dug shafts are drawn over the ground in a layer of their own, from `glyphs` (8 by 8 pixel rows, a palette of [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a], '.' clear); a node that has been gathered is not drawn until it regrows.
